title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 08 (Board Paper Standard III (Novel & Heroes))
subject: english-12

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'infinitesimal' as used in 'The Dying Sun'?

options.A: Microscopic
options.B: Minute
options.C: Colossal / Immense
options.D: Negligible

questions.explanation: 'Infinitesimal' means unimaginably small; its direct antonym is colossal, immense, or gigantic.

questions.question: According to Dean Hawkes, why do financial worries affect a student's mental performance?

options.A: Because banks charge high interest rates on credit cards
options.B: Anxiety over tuition bills and food expenses creates chronic psychological stress and distraction
options.C: Because poor students are not permitted into university libraries
options.D: Because textbooks cannot be bought on credit

questions.explanation: Worrying about where the next meal or tuition instalment will come from fractures a student's mental peace and focus.

questions.question: In 'End of Term', Daiches mentions that in later life, when he had his own money, what changed about his childhood desires?

options.A: He bought hundred tricycles and sweets immediately.
options.B: The intense longing had evaporated, proving that desires must be fulfilled in their proper time to bring true joy.
options.C: He opened a candy store in Edinburgh.
options.D: He gave all his money to the school.

questions.explanation: When an adult finally has money to purchase childhood toys, the magical childhood craving is gone forever.

questions.question: In 'The Man Who Was a Hospital', Jerome's pulse was beating at what ridiculous rate according to his self-examination?

options.A: It had stopped completely, or was racing at 147 beats a minute
options.B: Exactly 72 beats a minute
options.C: Around 50 beats a minute
options.D: His heart had shifted to his right ear

questions.explanation: He couldn't feel his pulse at first, then panicked and calculated it frantically at 147 beats per minute.

questions.question: In 'Hunger and Population', what biblical reference illustrates ancient famines?

options.A: The seven lean years of famine in Egypt interpreted by Joseph
options.B: The building of Noah's Ark
options.C: The destruction of Babylon
options.D: David and Goliath

questions.explanation: Pharaoh's dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows is cited as an ancient recorded famine in Egypt.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that uses the correct idiom:

options.A: He burned the midnight oil to prepare for his exams.
options.B: He boiled the midnight kerosene for his exams.
options.C: He lit the evening candle for his exams.
options.D: He roasted the midnight lamp for his exams.

questions.explanation: The correct English idiom for studying late into the night is 'to burn the midnight oil'.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled word:

options.A: Discernment
options.B: Descernment
options.C: Discerment
options.D: Discirnment

questions.explanation: 'Discernment' is spelled with 'sc' and 'ernment'.

questions.question: How did Churchill view his fellow Harrow classmates who had won prizes in Latin and Greek in their adult lives?

options.A: They became the sole rulers of the world.
options.B: Many had to learn ordinary English afterwards to earn their living or make their way in politics, proving his training was superior.
options.C: They all became professional athletes.
options.D: They forgot how to speak.

questions.explanation: In adult life, those who shone in Latin and Greek had to master practical English to communicate in the real world.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'serendipity' in scientific history?

options.A: Deliberate and planned mathematical calculation
options.B: The occurrence of valuable discoveries by happy chance or fortunate accident
options.C: Severe intellectual fatigue
options.D: Plagiarism of another's work

questions.explanation: 'Serendipity' is the fortunate discovery of something valuable while looking for something else, perfectly typified by Fleming's mould.

questions.question: Which of the following demonstrates correct use of the subjunctive mood?

options.A: It is essential that Fleming receives all the credit.
options.B: It is essential that Fleming receive all the credit.
options.C: It is essential that Fleming will receive all the credit.
options.D: It is essential that Fleming received all the credit.

questions.explanation: Subjunctive expressions ('it is essential that...') require the base form of the verb ('receive').

questions.question: In what way did Kemal reform primary and secondary education?

options.A: He unified all schools under the Ministry of National Education, establishing free, compulsory, co-educational scientific schooling.
options.B: He privatized all schools for wealthy elites.
options.C: He closed all rural village schools.
options.D: He banned science and mathematics.

questions.explanation: The Law of Unification of Instruction (1924) created a modern, secular, universal education system for both boys and girls.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the passive voice effectively to emphasize historical action?

options.A: The Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923 by the Grand National Assembly.
options.B: The Grand National Assembly proclaimed the Republic of Turkey.
options.C: They were proclaiming the Republic in 1923.
options.D: Proclamation of the republic happened.

questions.explanation: The passive construction highlights the momentous historic event ('The Republic of Turkey was proclaimed') as the primary subject.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech: 'Brookfield was like a little world in itself, sheltered from the stormy currents of modern life.'

options.A: Simile and metaphor
options.B: Oxymoron
options.C: Hyperbole
options.D: Synecdoche

questions.explanation: Comparing Brookfield to a little world using 'like' is an explicit simile accompanied by metaphorical sheltering.

questions.question: What is the overarching theme of Chapters 1 to 6 of 'Good-bye, Mr. Chips'?

options.A: The profound, humanizing power of true love and companionship over a dry, routine-bound life
options.B: The futility of secondary education
options.C: The superiority of industrial manufacturing over classical learning
options.D: A political critique of British imperial treaties

questions.explanation: Katherine's entrance into Chips' life humanized and elevated him, turning a dry pedagogue into a beloved, immortal school icon.

questions.question: What was the significance of the year 1913 in European history as well as Chips' personal life?

options.A: It was the final year of peaceful, sunny Edwardian tranquility before the cataclysm of World War I shattered European civilization.
options.B: The fall of the Roman Empire
options.C: The invention of printing press
options.D: The end of the French Revolution

questions.explanation: 1913 was the twilight of the peaceful pre-war Victorian/Edwardian world, shortly before the slaughter of WW1 began in August 1914.

questions.question: What catastrophic tragedy struck Mr. Chips on 1st April 1898 in Chapter 7?

options.A: Katherine and their newborn baby died during childbirth.
options.B: Brookfield School burned down completely.
options.C: Chips was dismissed by the Board of Governors.
options.D: He lost his vision in an explosion in the chemistry lab.

questions.explanation: On April Fools' Day 1898, Katherine and her infant child tragically died, leaving Chips heartbroken in profound silence.

questions.question: What did Cartwright mean when he said: 'He was Brookfield, and Brookfield was him'?

options.A: Chips had become the living embodiment of the school's history, soul, and moral traditions.
options.B: Chips legally owned the land.
options.C: The school was going to be demolished.
options.D: Chips was the only master left.

questions.explanation: Chips and Brookfield were inseparable in spirit; sixty-three years of association made him the school's immortal avatar.

questions.question: What was Chips' immediate response to Chatteris' plea for help in 1916?

options.A: He agreed immediately with quiet, patriotic joy, putting on his old tattered gown and returning to the classroom the very next morning.
options.B: He refused, claiming his health was too fragile.
options.C: He demanded double his old salary.
options.D: He advised Chatteris to hire German teachers.

questions.explanation: Chips was thrilled to be useful again; he stepped back into his old post with renewed youthful vigor and devotion.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: If I was you, I would consult Dr. Merivale immediately.
options.B: If I were you, I would consult Dr. Merivale immediately.
options.C: If I am you, I will consult Dr. Merivale.
options.D: If I had been you, I will consult Dr. Merivale.

questions.explanation: Hypothetical contrary-to-fact conditions require the subjunctive 'were' regardless of the subject pronoun.

questions.question: Choose the correct version of the sentence containing the indefinite pronoun 'one':

options.A: One must do his duty honestly at all times.
options.B: One must do one's duty honestly at all times.
options.C: One must do their duty honestly at all times.
options.D: One must do her duty honestly at all times.

questions.explanation: The pronoun 'one' must maintain consistency throughout the sentence; its possessive form is strictly 'one's'.
